new_objections_from_qa_round2_codex.claim_under_review: Decision 1 REVISION-2 field whitelist scans Glob.path, Glob.pattern, Grep.path, Grep.glob as INDEPENDENT fields. AC12 enumerates payloads where each field individually is path-shaped under denied prefix.
evidence_against: Real Glob/Grep tool semantics: pattern/glob is RELATIVE to path. The scanner must consider the joined candidate, not each field in isolation.

Concrete bypass example (Codex r2 verbatim): Glob(path:'/root/travel-planner/.claude/skills', pattern:'gaode-maps/**'). Field-by-field scan: Glob.path='/root/travel-planner/.claude/skills' does NOT contain '/.claude/skills/gaode-maps/' substring. Glob.pattern='gaode-maps/**' resolved via os.path.abspath from cwd does not start with '/.claude/skills/gaode-maps/' either. Both fields individually pass; the COMPOSED real glob target '/root/travel-planner/.claude/skills/gaode-maps/**' is what would actually be matched at filesystem level — and it would hit the denied prefix.

Same class for Grep: Grep(path:'/root/travel-planner/.claude/commands/scripts', glob:'gaode-maps/**/*.py', pattern:'x'). Field-by-field: neither Grep.path nor Grep.glob individually under denied prefix. Composed: '/root/travel-planner/.claude/commands/scripts/gaode-maps/**/*.py' would be denied.
AC12 sub-payloads (2), (3), (4) all use the SIMPLER form where the path-shaped string is in a single field — these PASS the field-whitelist scan but do NOT exercise the composed bypass class.
Codex r2 (gpt-5.5 xhigh reasoning) flagged this as critical: 'PASS is premature until at least points 1 and 2 are corrected.'
new_objections_from_qa_round2_codex.impact: REVISION-2 demonstrably introduces (or fails to close) a real Glob/Grep composed-path bypass class. The field-whitelist approach is an improvement over shape-based dispatch (which had its own AC12/AC15 inconsistency), but it left the path+pattern composition class uncovered. A banned subagent could trivially bypass the read-path matcher via Glob(path=parent, pattern=child-under-denied) — defeating the entire harness ban for the read-path surface for the most common Glob/Grep usage. This is a real 永久彻底修复 gap.
required_ba_revision: Decision 1 REVISION-2 must declare: when both Glob.path AND Glob.pattern are present, scanner constructs joined-candidate string (os.path.join(Glob.path, Glob.pattern) — or fnmatch synthesis) and feeds the joined candidate to read-path matcher. Same for Grep.path + Grep.glob.

AC12 must add explicit composed-path payloads: (a) Glob(path:'/root/travel-planner/.claude/skills', pattern:'gaode-maps/**') -> exit 2 surface:read-path (composed candidate matches denied prefix); (b) Grep(path:'/root/travel-planner/.claude/commands/scripts', glob:'gaode-maps/**/*.py', pattern:'x') -> exit 2 surface:read-path; (c) Negative: Glob(path:'/root/travel-planner', pattern:'data/**/*.json') -> NOT a gaode-policy deny.
T2 fixture set must include the 2 positive composed-path payloads above plus the negative regression-guard.
